newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks lock in another record close.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks lock in another record close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2634.0 +11 US 30yr cl 6.92 -0.06
10yrbond futs 92.605 +0.065 Gold NY 344.65 Lon fix 345.60
*Stocks lock in another record close but volumes moderate and investors selective. Volume 310.30 million, A$802.56 million value, 1,106 stocks traded, 334 steady, 393 up, 379 down.
Australian stocks bounded away in the afternoon to lock in another record close on Monday with the available investor interest clearly favouring the buy side.
The All Ordinaries Index added 15.2 points to 2,625.7, hitting a record high 2,626.0 on the way, surpassing Friday's previous high of 2,617.4.
The June share price index futures contract was 11 points up at 2,634, an 8.3 point premium to the underlying market.
Turnover was only moderate and buying interest was selective, with a strong preference for Friday's darlings, bellwether BHP and bank sector star ANZ.
ANZ saw solid activity with 4.9 million shares traded and the stock ended up 2.9 percent at A$9.25 after touching a record high of A$9.30. BHP rose 29.2 cents to A$19.15.
"ANZ is getting all the attention after its result last week and there is probably some switching in the group at the moment," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.

Where the broader impetus for the continued rally was coming from was unclear. Some suggested the old chestnut of Asian investors while others suspected the patchy moves were indicative of arbitrage activity remaining from last week.

"It could be some arbitrage activity but what I would call the real activity doesn't appear to be there to any extent. It's not wildly active," said Eric Gale, head of institutions at investment bank Ord Minnett.

Macquarie Bank Ltd closed four cents firmer at A$9.50 after equalling its record high of A$9.60. The investment bank reported a stronger than expected full year net profit of A$116.9 million and a final dividend of 25 cents per share.
Rio Tinto Ltd trailled its London shares lower, losing 18.1 cents to A$21.35.

Shares in oil and gas group Cultus Petroleum NL dipped 15 cents to A$3.75 after it issued a statement saying that in its opinion recovery rates at the Cornea oil field offshore Western Australia were likely to be better than those indicated last week by joint venture partner Shell Australia Ltd, a unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell group.
Rises slightly shaded falls, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade was lighter after Friday's heavy activity levels with 29,019 (71,538) options and 5,372 (7,972) June SPI contracts traded.
In other local markets, the Australian bond market cooled off after last Friday's heady rally which followed a weak retail trade report as the short end succumbed to profit-taking.
By 4.50 p.m. (0650 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.40 percent, down from Friday's 7.46 percent.
The Australian dollar delved beneath 76 cents to three month lows Monday as exporter support finally buckled beneath the burden of offshore selling.
By 4.50 p.m. (0650 GMT), the local dollar was lying low at US$0.7580/85, down from Friday's soft US$0.7604/09 close.
